escalations: The 1904-07 revival entry's own text is wrong beyond one sentence, not just unsupported. Its longDescription, why and legacy say the three revivals were 'unconnected' and that 'none of them descended from the others'. Helen Dyer's life of Pandita Ramabai (1913 edition, read online) says: when the news of the Welsh revival reached Ramabai, a new prayer circle was formed at Mukti in January 1905 to pray for revival in India, and news of the revival at the Welsh missions in the Assam hills encouraged it. The polygenesis framing runs through three fields and the legacy's closing argument, so it is left unchanged and flagged for the entry's owner. The claim that none came from Azusa Street still holds.

Method question. The era 10 cap lets an online church-body text lift a link to Widely Accepted, but Widely Accepted also needs a secondary work for the consensus reading. For four links (charismatic-mainline, Azusa-charismatic, Messianic Judaism-Hebrew Roots, Pyongyang revival-Korean Protestantism) the only secondary is repo-cited and named, not read, so it supports nothing beyond its title. I graded them Widely Accepted and flagged each. If a named-only secondary should not count, these four need a ruling on the right grade, since the primary evidence is direct and Inferential-Thin would understate it.
